Purpose and exclusions

One NPC may offer dialogue, quests, merchant, trainer and crafting services without duplicating player state. Conditions and choices are authored; lasting consequences are validated character records, not booleans hidden in a widget.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create URPGNPCDefinition and URPGDialogueDefinition schemas. Author NPC_Mara as quartermaster/quest giver/vendor and NPC_Tovin as banker/trainer contact with separate service IDs.
  2. Build DA_Dialogue_Mara with greeting, missing-supplies quest offer, in-progress reminder, ready-to-complete and completed nodes; include an optional reputation-sensitive branch.
  3. Create BP_NPC_Mara from ARPGServiceNPC with interaction and sprite presentation but no hostile AI requirement. Static and animated NPCs share service ownership rules.
  4. Build WBP_Dialogue with speaker name, text, option list, close and focus restoration; options are keyed by ID rather than array index alone.
  5. Reopen quest/vendor/trainer components to accept an NPC context and return explicit eligibility reasons; never copy quest inventory into the NPC actor.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in NPC roles, branching dialogue and consequence records. Rule owner: URPGDialogueComponent. This asset’s role is One NPC may offer dialogue, quests, merchant, trainer and crafting services without duplicating player state. Conditions and choices are authored; lasting consequences are validated character records, not booleans hidden in a widget.

  1. Player interacts within range/LOS; server resolves NPC roles and current condition facts, returning only available choices and a conversation nonce.
  2. UMG shows localized text/options and stores no authoritative quest/reputation variables.
  3. Player chooses an option ID; server re-evaluates conditions and node/nonce/version, since another action may have changed quest state.
  4. Pure conversation advances without an economic write; a lasting choice uses an idempotent backend command for consequence flags/reputation/reward as defined.
  5. Merchant/trainer/quest/craft option opens the relevant service context; that domain repeats validation for its eventual commit.
  6. Leaving range, NPC despawn, death or travel closes conversation, unbinds UI and invalidates nonce. Late replies from old zone generations are ignored.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / NPC_Mara / NPC_Tovin / Dialogue_RoadSupplies. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Choice condition changed after screen opened -> ConditionChanged and refreshed node; no unauthorized reward.
Option ID from another dialogue -> InvalidOption.
NPC disappears mid-command -> reversible conversation closes; committed consequence remains and receipt resolves.
Duplicate choice reward packet -> original receipt/AlreadyApplied.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
